t.1.52.1: Śaunaka said: The serpents who fell into the fire, the bearer of oblations, at this serpent sacrifice, I wish to hear the names of all of them, O son of a Sūta.
t.1.52.2: Many thousands, millions and tens of millions perished in it; they cannot be counted because of their great number, O best of those who know the Veda.
t.1.52.3: But learn from me, as I recall them, the names of the chief serpents that were offered as oblations into Jātavedas, as they are being told.
t.1.52.4: First learn from me, in order of their importance, those born in the lineage of Vāsuki: blue-red and white, terrible, huge-bodied, and virulent with poison.
t.1.52.5: Koṭika, Mānasa, Pūrṇa, Saha, Paila, Halīsaka, Picchila, Koṇapa, Cakra, Koṇavega, and Prakālana.
t.1.52.6: Hiraṇyavāha, Śaraṇa, Kakṣaka, and Kāladantaka: these Nāgas, born of Vāsuki, entered the bearer of oblations, the fire.
t.1.52.7: I shall tell you of those born in the lineage of Takṣaka; learn of them: Pucchaṇḍaka, Maṇḍalaka, Piṇḍabhettā, Rabheṇaka.
t.1.52.8: Ucchikha, Surasa, Draṅga, Balaheḍa, Virohaṇa, Śilīśalakara, Mūka, Sukumāra, and Pravepana.
t.1.52.9: Mudgara, Śaśaromā, Sumanā and Vegavāhana: these nāgas born of Takṣaka entered the oblation-bearing fire.
t.1.52.10: Pārāvata, Pāriyātra, Pāṇḍara, Hariṇa, Kṛśa, Vihaṃga, Śarabha, Moda, Pramoda, and Saṃhatāṅgada.
t.1.52.11: These, born of the lineage of Airāvata, entered the fire, the bearer of oblations. Now hear from me, O best of the twice-born, the serpents born of the lineage of Kauravya.
t.1.52.13: Hear now, O brahmin, the serpents born in the lineage of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, swift as the wind and virulent with poison, as I name them truly.
t.1.52.12: Aiṇḍila, Kuṇḍala, Muṇḍa, Veṇiskandha, Kumāraka, Bāhuka and Śṛṅgavega, Dhūrtaka, and the two, Pāta and Pātṛ.
t.1.52.14: Śaṅkukarṇa, Piṅgalaka, the pair Kuṭhāramukha and Mecaka, Pūrṇāṅgada, Pūrṇamukha, Prahasa, Śakuni, and Hari.
t.1.52.15: Āmāhaṭha, Komaṭhaka, Śvasana, Mānava, Vaṭa, Bhairava, Muṇḍavedāṅga, Piśaṅga, and Udrapāraga.
t.1.52.17: Varāhaka, Vāraṇaka, Sumitra, Citravedika, Parāśara, Taruṇaka, Maṇiskandha, and likewise Aruṇi.
t.1.52.16: Ṛṣabha, the one named Vegavant, Piṇḍāraka and Mahāhanu, Raktāṅga, Sarvasāraṅga, Samṛddha, and Pāṭa and Rākṣasa.
t.1.52.18: Thus, O brahman, I have named the Nāgas, those enhancers of renown, according to their eminence; but because of their great number, not all of them have been enumerated.
t.1.52.19: But the sons and grandsons of these, and the continuing line of their offspring, who went into the blazing fire, cannot be counted.
t.1.52.20: Seven-headed ones, two-headed ones, and others likewise five-headed, terrible, with venom like the fire of doom, were offered as oblations by hundreds of thousands.
t.1.52.22: Able to take any form at will and to go wherever they wished, dreadful with poison like blazing fire, they were burned there at that great sacrifice, crushed by the rod of brahmanical power.
t.1.52.21: Huge of body and mighty in strength, towering like mountain peaks, they were a yojana in length and breadth, and some stretched out to two yojanas.
